title: Claims-Based Algorithms for Identifying Patients With Pulmonary Hypertension: A Comparison of Decision Rules and Machine-Learning Approaches
summary: Claims-based machine-learning algorithms outperformed conventional decision rules for pulmonary-hypertension cohort ascertainment in a chart-reviewed gold-standard study. Gold-standard chart-reviewed cohort (386 PH, 164 non-PH) and reported AUC/sensitivity/specificity provide validation.
ai_technology: Methods describe claims-based lasso, random-forest and gradient-boosting models alongside decision rules.
organization: Harvard Medical School; Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Institute; Boston Children's Hospital

evidence.tested: Results compare machine-learning algorithms with decision rules for identifying pulmonary-hypertension cohorts.
evidence.unknown: Gold-standard chart-reviewed cohort (386 PH, 164 non-PH) and reported AUC/sensitivity/specificity provide validation. The source does not establish benefits beyond the reported evaluation.
evidence.ai_role: Methods describe claims-based lasso, random-forest and gradient-boosting models alongside decision rules.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
